name: Kenco Mead Johnson DC - Mount Vernon IN

fieldNotes.SITE_STATUS: FACILITY DESTROYED AND DEMOLISHED. An EF-3 tornado struck the Mead Johnson / Kenco DC on 9 Jul 2024, collapsing the roof and multiple walls. Current 2026 Maxar imagery and 2025-09 Street View show the warehouse fully razed to a bare concrete slab with exposed foundation footings and demolition debris. The site is non-operational. All operational classification fields are inferred from the surviving slab footprint and access roads, not a working yard.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm or guard structure visible at the NE entrance off the loop road; classified false but the pre-tornado state is unknowable from current imagery.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 25-50 band from the slab footprint and a dock-apron strip along the west/south face; the actual building no longer exists to count doors.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large paved loop-yard area north and east of the slab could function as trailer storage; marked true tentatively but no trailers present.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town along Highway 62 E surrounded by farmland; classified Rural.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: The racetrack-shaped tank/manufacturing complex to the SW is the separate Mead Johnson Mount Vernon manufacturing plant, not part of this DC parcel.
